extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys/agents, Patent Office officials, and lawyers handling U.S. patent matters
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted statutory standards from U.S. patent statutes governing who may obtain patents, what must be included in applications/specifications/drawings/models, procedural limits (fees, dates, time-to-prosecute), office duties, evidentiary rules, and related administrative rules. Focused on U.S. patent and design-patent rules appearing in the Revised Statutes and related Acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of Patent-Office Fees by Treasurer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasurer of the United States is authorized to pay back any sum or sums of money to any person (or receiver/depositary to the credit of the treasurer) as for fees accruing at the Patent Office through mistake, upon certificate thereof being made to said treasurer by the Commissioner of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory mechanism for refunding mistakenly paid Patent Office fees; requires certificate from the Commissioner. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4936 / Section 70.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Obtain a Design Patent (Design Patent Eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, by his own industry, genius, efforts, and expense, has invented or produced any new and original design for a manufacture (including bust, statue, alto-relievo, bas-relief, printing designs for fabrics, impressions, ornaments, patterns, prints, pictures, or any new, useful, and original shape or configuration of any article of manufacture), not having been known or used by others before his invention or produced, or patented or described in any printed publication, may obtain a patent for the same upon payment of the duty required by law and other due proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design must be new and original and not previously known, used, patented, or printed. Procedure for obtaining a design patent parallels that for inventions. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4929 / Section 71.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Models May Be Dispensed with for Designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may dispense with models of designs when the design can be sufficiently represented by drawings or photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows waiver of physical models for design patents where visual representations suffice. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4930 / Section 72.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Term Length Options for Design Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs may be granted for the term of three years and six months, or for seven years, or for fourteen years, as the applicant may elect in his application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant elects one of the statutory term options at application. Fee schedule corresponds to term chosen. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4931 / Section 73.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension for Pre-1861 Design Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentees of designs issued prior to March 2, 1861, are entitled to extension of their respective patents for the term of seven years in the same manner and under the same restrictions as provided for extensions of patents for inventions issued prior to March 2, 1861.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional rule for older design patents to obtain extension comparable to invention-patent extensions. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4932 / Section 74.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in Design Cases (Rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: For three years and six months, ten dollars; for seven years, fifteen dollars; for fourteen years, thirty dollars. For all other cases in which fees are required, the same rates as in cases of inventions or discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit statutory fee amounts for design patent terms; other fees follow invention schedule. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4934 / Section 75.]

rubrics_metrics.name: General Application of Patent Provisions to Designs
rubrics_metrics.description: All the regulations and provisions which apply to obtaining or protection of patents for inventions or discoveries, not inconsistent with the provisions of this act, shall apply to patents for designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design-patent practice generally follows the patent rules for inventions, except where inconsistent. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4933 / Section 76.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office May Print and Distribute Certified Copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to have printed, for gratuitous distribution not to exceed 150 copies, the complete specifications and drawings of each patent thereafter issued with suitable indexes; one copy to be placed in each State and Territory capitol, one in each district-court clerk's office (except when located in capitols), and one in the Library of Congress. These copies shall be certified under the Commissioner's hand and seal and not be taken from depositories except to be used as evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized public depositories of certified patent copies; certified copies are intended for evidence use and public inspection. [See Revised Statutes, Section 490.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Sale and Furnishing of Additional Certified Copies and Sets
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may have printed additional copies of specifications and drawings, certified as provided, at a price not to exceed the contract price for such drawings for sale as warranted by actual demand; he may furnish a complete set to any public library that will pay for binding and transportation and provide proper custody and public access under reasonable regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism for selling certified copies and supplying libraries if conditions satisfied. [See Revised Statutes, Section 491.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement of Lithographing and Engraving
rubrics_metrics.description: Lithographing and engraving required by the printing sections shall be awarded to the lowest and best bidders for the interest of the Government, with due regard to execution of the work, after due advertising by the Congressional Printer under direction of the Joint Committee on Printing; the Joint Committee may empower the Congressional Printer to make immediate contracts when exigencies of public service justify it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement standard: lowest and best bidder, subject to execution quality and possible exceptions for urgency. [See Revised Statutes, Section 492.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Price Limits for Uncertified Printed Copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The price of printed copies of specifications and drawings of patents, when uncertified, shall be determined by the Commissioner of Patents, ten cents being fixed as the minimum and fifty cents as the maximum price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner sets actual price within statutory bounds for uncertified copies. Certified copies have separate pricing rules. [See Revised Statutes, Section 493 (and prior Act).]

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of Patent-Office Records as Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Written or printed copies of any records, books, papers, or drawings belonging to the Patent-Office, and letters-patent authenticated by the seal and certified by the Commissioner, shall be evidence in all cases wherein the originals could be evidence; applicants paying the fee required shall have certified copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified and authenticated Patent Office copies are admissible as evidence in court. [See Revised Statutes, Section 892.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified Copies of Foreign Patents as Prima-Facie Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the specifications and drawings of foreign letters-patent, certified as provided, shall be prima-facie evidence of the fact of the granting of such letters-patent, and of the date and contents thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign patent documents, when certified by Patent Office, carry evidentiary presumptions. [See Revised Statutes, Section 893.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed/Certified Patent Copies in Courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed copies of specifications and drawings of patents that the Commissioner is authorized to print and deposit in state/territorial capitols and clerk's offices, when certified and authenticated by his seal, shall be received in all courts as evidence of all matters contained therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces evidentiary status of certified printed patent copies for judicial proceedings. [See Revised Statutes, Section 894 and Joint Resolution cited.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner and Patent-Office Officers: Appointments and Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be in the Patent Office a Commissioner of Patents, one Assistant Commissioner, and three examiners-in-chief appointed by the President with Senate advice and consent; other officers, clerks, and employees appointed by the Secretary of the Interior upon nomination by the Commissioner. The Commissioner shall superintend duties respecting granting and issuing patents and have charge of all books, records, papers, models, machines, and other things belonging to the Patent-Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes office structure, appointment authority, and the Commissioner's supervisory responsibilities. [See Revised Statutes, Sections 476 and 481.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal of the Patent-Office and Authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: The seal heretofore provided for the Patent-Office shall be the seal of the Office, with which letters-patent and papers issued from the Office shall be authenticated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentication of patents and official papers is by the Patent-Office seal. [See Revised Statutes, Section 478.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds for Commissioner and Chief Clerk
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents and the chief clerk, before entering upon their duties, shall severally give bond with sureties to the Treasurer of the United States, the former in the sum of $10,000 and the latter in the sum of $5,000, conditioned for faithful discharge of duties and rendering true accounts of money received by virtue of their offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial accountability requirements for senior Patent Office officers. [See Revised Statutes, Section 479.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on Officers and Employees Acquiring Patent Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: All officers and employees of the Patent-Office shall be incapable, during the period for which they hold their appointments, of acquiring or taking, directly or indirectly (except by inheritance or bequest), any right or interest in any patent issued by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict-of-interest prohibition preventing Patent Office personnel from holding patent interests while in office. [See Revised Statutes, Section 480.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and Duties of Examiners-in-Chief
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners-in-chief shall be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability; their duty is, on written petition of the appellant, to revise and determine upon the validity of adverse decisions of examiners upon applications for patents and re-issues, and in interference cases; when required by the Commissioner, they shall hear and report upon claims for extensions and perform other like duties assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets qualification standard (legal + scientific competency) and appellate/review responsibilities for senior examiners. [See Revised Statutes, Section 482.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner May Establish Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents, subject to approval of the Secretary of the Interior, may from time to time establish regulations, not inconsistent with law, for the conduct of proceedings in the Patent-Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation of rulemaking authority for office procedures, constrained by law and Secretary approval. [See Revised Statutes, Section 483.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and Public Exhibition of Models and Specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall cause models, specimens of composition, fabrics, manufactures, works of art, and designs deposited in the Patent-Office to be classified and arranged in suitable cases and kept open during suitable hours for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates public accessibility and proper classification of deposited materials for inspection. [See Revised Statutes, Section 484.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of Models from Rejected Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may restore to applicants such models belonging to rejected applications as he shall not think necessary to preserve; he may sell or otherwise dispose of them after the application has been finally rejected for one year, paying proceeds into the Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and timing (one-year waiting period after final rejection) for returning or disposing of models from rejected applications. [See Revised Statutes, Section 485.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-Office Library Acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be purchased for Patent-Office use a library of scientific works and periodicals, foreign and American, as may aid officers in discharge of duties, not exceeding annual appropriation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision for maintaining reference resources to support examination work. [See Revised Statutes, Section 486.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to Recognize Patent Agents for Gross Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: For gross misconduct the Commissioner may refuse to recognize any person as a patent-agent, either generally or in any particular case; reasons must be duly recorded and subject to approval of the Secretary of the Interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement mechanism against agent misconduct, with recorded reasons and oversight. [See Revised Statutes, Section 487.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Print Illegible Papers at Party Cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may require all papers filed in the Patent-Office, if not correctly, legibly, and clearly written, to be printed at the cost of the party filing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative sanction to ensure legibility of filings and to shift printing cost to filer when necessary. [See Revised Statutes, Section 488.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing of Claims, Laws, Decisions for Public Information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may print, or cause to be printed, copies of the claims of current issues and copies of such laws, decisions, regulations, and circulars as may be necessary for the information of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority to publish materials to inform practitioners and the public about patent claims and governing law. [See Revised Statutes, Section 489.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Report Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall lay before Congress annually a report giving a detailed statement of all moneys received for patents and other sources, detailed expenditures for contingent and miscellaneous expenses, list of patents granted during the year with subjects, alphabetical list of patentees with residences, list of patents extended during the year, and such other information of the condition of the Patent-Office as may be useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory reporting content intended to inform Congress and the public on Patent Office finances and activity. [See Revised Statutes, Section 494.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursement Responsibility for Patent-Office
rubrics_metrics.description: All disbursements for the Patent-Office shall be made by the disbursing clerk of the Interior Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies financial disbursement channel for Patent Office expenditures. [See Revised Statutes, Section 496.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Courts Jurisdiction Over Patent Suits
rubrics_metrics.description: Circuit courts shall have original jurisdiction of all suits at law and in equity arising under the patent or copyright laws of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines federal-court jurisdiction for patent litigation. [See Revised Statutes, Section 629.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals/Writs of Error in Patent Cases Without Regard to Amount
rubrics_metrics.description: A writ of error may be allowed to review any final judgment at law, and an appeal shall be allowed from any final decree in equity mentioned, without regard to the sum or value in dispute, for final judgments or decrees touching patent-rights or copyrights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure enabling appellate review of patent cases irrespective of monetary amount involved. [See Revised Statutes, Section 699.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs Limitation Where Patentee Falsely Claims Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: When judgment or decree is rendered for infringement of part of a patent in which it appears the patentee in his specification claimed to be the original and first inventor of any material or substantial part of the thing patented of which he was not the original and first inventor, no costs shall be recovered unless the proper disclaimer has been entered at the Patent-Office before the suit was brought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adverse-costs rule to discourage erroneous or false originality claims; requires pre-suit disclaimer to preserve costs. [See Revised Statutes, Section 973.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Issuance, Attestation, and Recording
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents shall be issued in the name of the United States under the seal of the Patent Office, signed by the Secretary of the Interior and countersigned by the Commissioner, and shall be recorded, together with the specifications, in books kept for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities for patent issuance and official recording, important for validity and public record. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4883.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Contents and Term (Short Title; Grant; Annexation of Spec)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall contain a short title or description of the invention or discovery, correctly indicating its nature and design, and a grant to the patentee, his heirs or assigns, for the term of seventeen years, of the exclusive right to make, use, and vend the invention throughout the United States and Territories, referring to the specification for particulars; a copy of the specification and drawings shall be annexed and be part of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies essential patent contents (short title, grant language, 17-year term, annexed spec/drawings) required for the patent document. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4884.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of Patent and Payment of Final Fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall bear date as of a day not later than six months from the time at which it was passed and allowed and notice was sent to the applicant or his agent; if the final fee is not paid within that period the patent shall be withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tenor on dating patents and link to timely payment of final fee (six-month limit). [See Revised Statutes, Section 4885.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable Subject Matter and Novelty/Utility Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has invented or discovered any new and useful art, machine, manufacture or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement thereof, not known or used by others in this country, and not patented or described in any printed publication in this or any foreign country before his invention or discovery, and not in public use or on sale for more than two years prior to his application (unless proved abandoned), may obtain a patent upon payment of fees and due proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core patentability requirements: novelty (no prior printed publication or prior known use in country), utility/usefulness, and bar for public use/sale over two years (statutory on-sale/public-use bar), subject to abandonment exceptions. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4886.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Prior Foreign Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be debarred from receiving a patent by reason of its having been first patented in a foreign country, unless it has been introduced into public use in the United States for more than two years prior to the application; but any U.S. patent granted for an invention previously patented abroad shall be limited to expire at the same time as the foreign patent (or the shortest if multiple), and in no case in force more than seventeen years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits U.S. patenting despite foreign patenting subject to U.S. public-use bar and term alignment with foreign patent term. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4887.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification Requisites: Written Application and Enabling Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Before receiving a patent the inventor shall make application in writing to the Commissioner and file in the Patent-Office a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making, constructing, compounding, and using it in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art or science to which it pertains to make, construct, compound, and use the same; in case of a machine, explain its principle and the best mode contemplated of applying that principle so as to distinguish it from other inventions; particularly point out and distinctly claim the part, improvement, or combination which he claims as his invention; the specification and claim shall be signed by the inventor and attested by two witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains written-application, enablement, best mode, written-claiming, signature, and witness-attestation requirements—fundamental for statutory sufficiency of the specification and claims. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4888.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings When Required and Filing Formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: When the nature of the case admits of drawings, the applicant shall furnish one copy signed by the inventor or his attorney in fact and attested by two witnesses, which shall be filed in the Patent-Office, and a copy of the drawing furnished by the Patent-Office shall be attached to the patent as part of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates signed/attested drawings when applicable and ensures a drawing copy is attached to the issued patent. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4889.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens for Compositions May Be Required
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention is of a composition of matter, the applicant, if required by the Commissioner, shall furnish specimens of ingredients and of the composition sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner discretion to require physical specimens for chemical/composition inventions to facilitate examination and testing. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4890.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Models May Be Required
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases which admit of representation by model, the applicant, if required by the Commissioner, shall furnish a model of convenient size to exhibit advantageously the several parts of his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may require models for inventions where a model aids understanding; models must be of convenient size to show parts. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4891.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of Applicant as to Originality and Citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall make oath that he does verily believe himself to be the original and first inventor or discoverer of the subject for which he solicits a patent; that he does not know and does not believe the same was ever before known or used; and shall state his country of citizenship. The oath may be made before authorized persons in the U.S. or, if the applicant resides abroad, before U.S. ministers, consuls, commercial agents, or foreign notaries as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sworn statement of originality and citizenship is required; foreign applicants may swear before specified foreign officials. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4892.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination and Issuance Standard: Utility and Entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing and payment of fees the Commissioner shall cause an examination to be made of the alleged new invention or discovery; if on such examination it appears the claimant is justly entitled to a patent under the law, and that the same is sufficiently useful and important, the Commissioner shall issue a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner's substantive gatekeeping role: entitlement under law plus sufficient usefulness/importance are required for issuance. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4893.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Limit to Complete Application (Two-Year Rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications for patents shall be completed and prepared for examination within two years after filing; failure to do so, or failure to prosecute within two years after any action therein of which notice was given, will result in the application being regarded as abandoned unless delay is shown to be unavoidable to the satisfaction of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-year prosecution/completion time limit with possible exception for unavoidable delay demonstrated to Commissioner's satisfaction. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4894.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents to Assignees and Sworn Specification Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be granted or re-issued to the assignee of the inventor, but the assignment must first be entered of record in the Patent-Office. In all cases of application by an assignee for issue of a patent, the application shall be made and the specification sworn to by the inventor or discoverer; in re-issue cases the corrected specification must be made and signed by the inventor or discoverer if living, unless the patent was issued and the assignment made before July 8, 1870.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects inventor's involvement in assignee-filed applications by requiring inventor's oath/signature except for specified historical exception. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4895.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of Executor/Administrator When Inventor Dies
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor dies before a patent is granted, the right of applying for and obtaining the patent devolves on his executor or administrator in trust for heirs or devisees as appropriate; when application is made by such legal representatives, the oath/affirmation required shall be varied in form so it can be made by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for post-mortem prosecution of patent rights and accommodation of required oath for legal representatives. [See Revised Statutes, Section 4896.]
